overall.summary: HPE's September 2025 10-Q filing has dropped virtually its entire detailed Risk Factors section relative to the June 2025 filing, eliminating extensive disclosures across at least 10 material risk categories including supply chain, geopolitical, cost/margin, revenue performance, regulatory/legal, liquidity, and financial sustainability topics. This is not selective trimming—it represents a wholesale removal of detailed, specific, and in some cases quantified risk disclosures (including a $1.4B goodwill impairment reference and specific AI order cancellation risks) during a period when many of these risks have intensified rather than abated. The pattern is consistent with either a filing error, a shift to reference-only risk factors pointing to the annual 10-K, or deliberate disclosure reduction that warrants immediate investigation.

Disappearance of the $1.4B Hybrid Cloud goodwill impairment disclosure and forward-looking impairment risk language, which may obscure ongoing asset quality concerns

Elimination of specific disclosures about AI order cancellation/de-booking risks, uneven demand digestion, extended payment terms for AI systems, and working capital strain—all critical to evaluating HPE's AI growth trajectory
